chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The boundary of the 'Aqiq (a cut in the neck for slaughter) is its beginning, the slaughter site (Maslakh), and its end is the one with the vein (Dhat 'Irnq).'

key_terms.الْعَقِيق: The act of slaughter or the specific cut made in the throat; here referring to the boundaries of the cut.
key_terms.الْمَسْلَخ: The slaughter site or the place where the cut is initiated, typically the throat.
key_terms.ذَاتُ عِرْقٍ: The area of the neck containing the main vein/artery, indicating the depth or extent of the cut required.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific anatomical boundaries for valid ritual slaughter in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* precisely delineates the anatomical limits for ritual slaughter, specifying the start at the 'Maslakh' (throat) and the end at 'Dhat al-'Irnq' (the neck's main vein). This definition ensures the validity of the cut by guaranteeing the severance of the primary vessels, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for lawful consumption. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on precision in ritual acts to maintain both spiritual and physical purity.
